hints: Substitute $h = 18 - r$ into $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$ to show $V = 6\pi r^2 - \frac{1}{3}\pi r^3$.
walkthrough:
Substitute $h = 18 - r$ into the cone volume formula:
$$V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2(18 - r) = 6\pi r^2 - \frac{1}{3}\pi r^3$$

hints: Differentiate $\frac{dV}{dr} = 12\pi r - \pi r^2 = \pi r(12 - r) = 0 \implies r = 12$.
walkthrough:
Differentiate $V$ with respect to $r$ and set equal to zero:
$$\frac{dV}{dr} = 12\pi r - \pi r^2 = \pi r(12 - r) = 0$$
Since $r$ is non-zero, $r = 12\text{ cm}$.

Differentiate a second time to determine the nature of the stationary point:
$$\frac{d^2V}{dr^2} = 12\pi - 2\pi r$$
$$\left.\frac{d^2V}{dr^2}\right|_{r=12} = 12\pi - 2\pi(12) = -12\pi < 0$$
Since the second derivative is strictly negative, the stationary value is a **maximum**.

Substitute $r = 12\text{ cm}$ into the volume formula:
$$V = 6\pi(12^2) - \frac{1}{3}\pi(12^3) = 6\pi(144) - \frac{1}{3}\pi(1728) = 864\pi - 576\pi = 288\pi\text{ cm}^3 \quad (\approx 905\text{ cm}^3)$$
